subject: Computer Networks
title: Discover Packet Routing
description: Discover how a packet travels through routers toward its destination.

mission.title: Route a Packet
mission.description: Follow one packet as routers choose a path from Computer A to Server C.

quiz.question: A packet reaches a router. What does the router mainly use to decide where to forward it?

discovery.title: Routers Forward by Destination
discovery.summary: Routers examine destination information and forward packets along a path toward their destination.

sections.title: What is a packet?
sections.content: A packet is a small piece of data sent across a network. Large messages are often split into many packets.

sections.title: What is a router?
sections.content: A router connects networks and forwards packets toward the network where they need to go.

sections.title: Source and destination
sections.content: The source sends the packet. The destination is the device or network the packet is trying to reach.

sections.title: What routing means
sections.content: Routing is the process of choosing a path for a packet through connected networks.

sections.title: Why routers choose paths
sections.content: A router can have more than one outgoing path, so it uses destination information to choose the useful next hop.

sections.title: IP address idea
sections.content: An IP address is a network address that helps identify where a packet should be delivered.

sections.title: Router and end device
sections.content: Computers and servers are end devices that send or receive data. Routers mainly move packets between networks.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of a parcel journey
alternate_explanations.content: A packet is like a parcel moving through sorting centers. Each router reads the destination and forwards it toward the correct next center.

alternate_explanations.title: Follow this packet
alternate_explanations.content: The packet starts at Computer A, reaches Router 1, and Router 1 chooses Router 3 instead of Router 2. Router 3 then forwards it to Server C.

introduction.title: Meet Packet Routing
introduction.content: Data crosses a network in small packets. Routers read a packet's destination and choose a useful next stop on the way there.
points: Computer A is the source sending this packet.
Server C is the destination that should receive it.
You will follow the packet as routers choose its path.

worked_example.title: Follow one packet
worked_example.content: The packet does not jump directly to the server; it travels through connected network devices.

steps.explanation: Computer A sends a packet toward its first router.
Router 1 examines the destination, Server C, and chooses the next hop that leads toward it.
Router 3 forwards the packet to the destination server.

worked_example.conclusion: Routers use destination information to forward packets one hop at a time.

next.title: Route the packet below.
next.content: Use NEXT STEP to see the possible paths before Router 1 makes its choice.

action_explanations.send-packet: The packet begins its journey at the source, Computer A, and heads to the first router.
action_explanations.reach-first-router: Router 1 now holds the packet and must choose the next hop toward Server C.
action_explanations.choose-correct-route: Router 3 is selected because it is the visible path that continues toward Server C.
action_explanations.forward-packet: The packet moves to Router 3, the next device on its chosen route.
action_explanations.reach-destination: Server C receives the packet because every router forwarded it toward the destination.

challenge.title: Packet Routing Challenge
challenge.start_message: Deliver a packet from Computer A to Server C while paying attention to the router's route choice.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Keep stepping through the network to follow the route again.

phases.title: Deliver the packet
phases.instruction: Move the packet through Router 1, choose the path toward Server C, and complete delivery.

target.label: Goal
target.description: Use the path Computer A → Router 1 → Router 3 → Server C; Router 2 should remain a visible unchosen option.

phases.feedback: At Router 1, inspect the destination and choose the next hop that leads toward Server C.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, what does a router use to decide where to forward a packet?
recall.empty_message: Write a short explanation before submitting.
recall.model_answer: A router examines the packet's destination network or address information and chooses the next connected path that moves the packet toward that destination.

guidance.start_message: Choose the next hop that moves the packet toward Server C.

items.content: At Router 1, choose the branch connected to the requested destination server.

phases.title: Route to Server C
phases.instruction: Forward the packet to Server C one correct hop at a time.

target.label: TARGET
target.description: Computer A → Router 1 → Router 3 → Server C

phases.feedback: Check the current node and the requested destination before choosing.

guidance.start_message: Route to a different destination with less guidance.

items.content: The correct Router 1 branch depends on the destination, not on which router looks closer.

phases.title: Route to Server B
phases.instruction: Choose the path that reaches Server B without a route recipe.
phases.feedback: A router chooses the next hop using destination information.

guidance.start_message: Choose a complete valid route without hints.

phases.title: Solve the route
phases.instruction: Deliver the packet with no guidance or displayed chosen path.
phases.feedback: A valid next hop must be connected and move toward the destination.

guidance.start_message: The destination is randomized. Plan the valid route without hints.

phases.title: Master an unfamiliar route
phases.instruction: Deliver the packet through the randomized valid topology path.

target.label: TARGET
target.description: Use the destination to choose each next hop.

phases.feedback: Keep other visible paths as distractors; only one route reaches the destination.

thinking.title: Plan the packet route
thinking.instruction: Predict the complete path and destination reachability before the packet moves.
thinking.do_not_execute: Do not forward the packet yet. Plan every hop in your head.

prediction_fields.label: Full route
prediction_fields.prompt: List node IDs from computer-a to the destination.

solve.title: Expert Packet Routing
solve.instruction: Deliver the randomized packet with no hints. Valid route reasoning is the score.
solve.operation_rule: Each selected hop must be connected and lead toward the destination.
solve.feedback: Use the destination to choose the correct next hop.
solve.solved_result: The packet reached the randomized destination.
